data.analysis: Keep N=3 and the same roles. Revise T1 because parallelizing only coarse roots assumes that stage supplies enough balanced work; the source also has an independent base-level depth scan. Revise T2 to test the existing light-count subdivision cutoff: with a threshold of 1, every nonempty tile continues subdividing to the leaves, which may trade excess culling for shading work. These are experiments, not known bottlenecks. T3 already has a distinct, well-scoped kernel objective, so no revision is justified for it.

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare parallel work decomposition while preserving the requested thread budget: worksharing the independent coarse-root tiles (including static versus dynamic scheduling) and parallelizing the independent base-level depth-bound rows in MinMaxZTree::Update. Measure each approach independently and, if useful, measure a combination rather than assuming additive gains; higher tree levels still depend on completed lower levels. Keep culling and shading algorithms unchanged, pass run()'s thread count as an upper bound, avoid unnecessary overhead at one thread, and preserve disjoint writes. Validate full output and correctness at 1 and 4 cores, including altered light colors.
revisions.subject: Parallelize independent coarse tiles within the requested thread budget

revisions.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate reducing recursive culling and hierarchy work in MinMaxZTree, SplitTileMinMax, IntersectLightsWithTileMinMax, and traversal. In addition to tile granularity and conservative plane-test optimizations, compare stopping subdivision for tiles with small nonzero light lists against continuing to the leaves; measure saved traversal/culling against the added per-pixel light work. Preserve conservative culling, current-frame depth-bound recomputation, and correctness for dimensions not supported by a chosen tile layout. Do not add parallelism or change ShadeTileC in this branch. Validate both core counts and altered light colors.
revisions.subject: Reduce recursive hierarchy and conservative light-culling overhead

data.shared_assumptions: The only automatic result is a correct baseline with three samples averaging 0.11495154 s; there are no per-core measurements, profiles, or candidate comparisons. The source's 16x16 base tiles and five levels imply 15 coarse roots for the supplied 1280x720 frame, but balance and speedup remain unmeasured. Source costs are hypotheses. Preserve the ABI, output, tolerance, and per-invocation depth/lighting work; evaluate all approaches under the frozen 1- and 4-core protocol. The observation does not establish whether timing samples are cold or warm relative to the source's lazy tree allocation, so follow the official harness rather than assuming either.
